editorial:
Picture this: a smooth-talking con artist gets himself locked up in a tiny police station just to hide from a killer. Sounds crazy, right? That is the wild setup of Copshop, a gritty thriller that traps you inside one building for most of its runtime. Gerard Butler plays the hit man who shows up at the precinct, while Frank Grillo is the slippery con artist trying to stay alive. The real star, though, is Alexis Louder as the rookie cop who suddenly has to deal with both of them. The movie has a fun, old-school action feel with sharp dialogue and a tense atmosphere that keeps you guessing about who you can trust.

The action is punchy and well-staged, and the cast clearly has a blast chewing on the script. Butler brings his usual tough-guy energy, Grillo is slippery and fun, and Louder holds her own as the heart of the story. The pacing rarely slows down, though the plot can feel a bit messy in the middle. If you enjoy single-location thrillers with attitude, this one is a blast.
endingExplained: In the final act, the police station erupts into chaos as multiple killers arrive. The rookie cop realizes the con artist has been playing everyone. She takes charge, outsmarting both the hit man and the con artist. The con artist tries to escape but is stopped. The rookie survives the shootout and walks away as the true hero, having proven herself under fire. The hit man's fate is left ambiguous, but the con artist is finally caught.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves single-location thrillers with attitude
